newsitem.title: JAPAN: Record amount of samurai bonds issued in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Record amount of samurai bonds issued in 1996.

text.p: A record 3.92 trillion yen worth of samurai bonds were issued in 1996, more than double the previous high of about 1.62 trillion yen in 1995, underwriting sources said on Tuesday.

Japanese retail investors' appetite for dual currency samurai bonds was huge throughout 1996 as they were eager to buy the bonds which offered high coupons at a time of ultra-low domestic interest rates, they said.
Of the total, about 2.4 trillion yen were dual currency samurais, up sharply from the previous record of about 600 billion yen in 1995.
Underwriters said the dual-currency samurais were popular among retail investors, especially because the coupons were paid in yen.
The underwriters said most of the dual currency samurai bonds were yen/Australian dollar ones, followed by yen/U.S. dollar and yen/New Zealand dollar.
"Demand from Japanese investors for the high coupon dual-currency issues pushed up the issuing volume to the record high," said Masaru Hamazaki, deputy manager at Yamaichi Research Institute.
Samurai bond issues of sub-investment grade, which means a credit rating of below double B plus (BB+), amounted to about 620 billion yen.
Japan's Ministry of Finance abolished samurai bond eligibility standards in January 1996. The move opened the door for foreign issuers with low credit ratings.
Issuers such as Argentina, Mexico, Brazil, Turkey and the Romanian central bank, all with sub-investment ratings, issued samurais after the MOF's deregulations.

Hamazaki said the samurai issuing volume could shrink this year as borrowers may face difficulties offering coupons high enough to attract retail investors, particularly after the recent falls in Australian and U.S. interest rates.
"Sub-investment grade samurai bonds are also not very popular among Japanese retail investors," Hamazaki said.

Issue volumes totalled more than 300 billion yen each month since June with December hitting 452.2 billion yen, the second highest ever after the 520 billion yen worth issued in February 1993, underwriters said. -- Chikafumi Hodo, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
